Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment is a peptidomics study focusing on proteasome-catalyzed peptide splicing (PCPS). While it discusses the immunopeptidome and HLA-I bound peptides, the actual MS runs were performed on in vitro digests of synthetic polypeptides, not MHC-enriched samples. The acquisition is DDA (Top Speed mode). Labeling is LFQ as no tags are mentioned and intensity values were used for abundance. PRIDE metadata lists 'Top-down proteomics' as an experiment type, but the methods describe a bottom-up-like peptidomics approach (digesting polypeptides into oligopeptides) using de novo sequencing.

Standard bottom-up pipelines will fail to identify the spliced peptides as they are non-contiguous. The 'preferred_engine' is set to peptide level because the analysis focuses on the abundance and length of specific spliced vs non-spliced peptide sequences.
